content.title: About
content.content: The Double cheeseburger from Burger King is a classic burger featuring two beef patties, two slices of cheese, pickles, onions, ketchup and mustard, all sandwiched between a soft sesame seed bun.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Double cheeseburger was introduced to the Burger King menu in the early 2000s as a response to growing demand for a more "meaty" option.
The burger contains roughly 450 kcal, making it more calorie‑dense than a standard cheeseburger.
The core ingredients stay the same worldwide, though minor regional variations exist.
In some markets Burger King offers a version with extra BBQ sauce or bacon.
The sesame bun is lightly toasted to give it a subtle nutty aroma.

items.title: Protein
items.content: Two beef patties provide about 30 g of high‑quality protein, essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Calcium
items.content: The cheese adds calcium, which supports bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Beef supplies vitamin B12 and B6, important for nervous system function.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Red meat is a good source of readily absorbable iron, needed for blood formation.

items.title: Energy
items.content: The combination of calories, protein, and fat makes the burger a quick source of energy.

items.title: High calorie and fat content
items.content: The large amount of calories and saturated fat can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Sodium level
items.content: Ketchup, mustard and processed ingredients raise the sodium content, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Allergens
items.content: The burger contains dairy (cheese), gluten (bun) and may have soy traces in sauces.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: Undercooked beef poses a risk of salmonella or other bacterial contamination.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The Double cheeseburger is typically served in its branded wrapper. Eat it by hand, often accompanied by fries and a drink. You can customize with extra sauce, vegetables, or request a gluten‑free bun.

content.title: Storage
content.content: If not consumed immediately, store the burger in a sealed container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat using an oven or grill to keep the bun from becoming soggy.
